questions.question: Which state is famous for Dandiya-ras dance?
questions.solution:
Dandiya Raas is the socio-religious folk dance of Gujarat, traditionally performed during the festival of Navratri.
  • The dance is performed with pairs of polished wooden sticks called Dandiyas, which represent the swords of Goddess Durga.
  • It depicts a mock-fight between the Goddess and the demon-king Mahishasura.
  • Note: While Garba is performed in circles with hand clapping, Dandiya Raas specifically utilizes the sticks for rhythmic striking.

questions.question: Which classical dance-drama from Kerala is renowned for its vibrant makeup, elaborate costumes, and exaggerated facial expressions, often depicting stories from the Ramayana?
questions.solution:
Kathakali is the world-famous classical dance-drama from Kerala characterized by its Vesham (costumes) and Aharya (makeup).
  • The makeup is color-coded to represent character traits: Pacha (Green) for noble heroes, Kathi (Knife) for royalty with evil streaks, and Thadi (Beard) for aggressive or demonic characters.
  • It is a 'total theatre' involving Mudras (hand gestures) and Navarasas (nine facial expressions).
  • Additional Info: It traditionally draws its themes from the Puranas, Ramayana, and Mahabharata.

questions.question: The couple who won Padma Bhushan in 2009 for Bharatanatyam are ___________ .
questions.option_1: Vannadil Pudiyaveettil Dhananjayan and Shanta Dhananjayan
questions.option_3: K-V. Sampath Kumar and Vidushi K-S. Jayalakshmi
questions.solution:
Vannadil Pudiyaveettil Dhananjayan and Shanta Dhananjayan, popularly known as the Dhananjayans, were awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2009.
  • They are a legendary dancing couple who graduated from Kalakshetra and are credited with popularizing the duo performance format in Bharatanatyam.
  • They founded the dance academy 'Bharata Kalanjali' in Chennai to preserve the purity of the art form.

questions.question: Who of the following was one of the stalwarts of a renaissance in Koodiyattam?
questions.solution:
Ammannur Madhava Chakyar was a legendary figure and a stalwart who led the renaissance of Koodiyattam.
  • Koodiyattam is the oldest surviving Sanskrit theatre tradition, native to Kerala, and is recognized by UNESCO as a Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity.
  • Chakyar is credited with bringing this ancient temple art form out of the 'Koothambalams' (temple theaters) to a wider global audience.
  • Note: His mastery over Netra-abhinaya (eye expressions) was considered unparalleled.

questions.question: Kuchipudi originated in a village named Kuchipudi in the Indian state of ___________ .
questions.solution:
Kuchipudi is a classical dance form that originated in the Kuchipudi village in the Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh.
  • It was originally a male-oriented dance-drama tradition (Bhagavata Mela) until it was refined into a solo dance form in the 20th century.
  • A unique feature of Kuchipudi is Tarangam, where the dancer performs while balancing on the rim of a brass plate.
  • Fact: It is characterized by fast-paced footwork and expressive 'Abhinaya' (acting).

questions.question: Who is often referred to as the "Mother of Modern Bharatanatyam"?
questions.solution:
Rukmini Devi Arundale is often referred to as the 'Mother of Modern Bharatanatyam' for her role in reviving the dance form.
  • She was instrumental in removing the social stigma associated with the dance (then known as Sadhir) and giving it global respectability.
  • She founded the Kalakshetra Foundation in Adyar, Chennai, which became the premier institute for learning classical arts.
  • Note: She was the first woman in Indian history to be nominated as a member of the Rajya Sabha.
